📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s a tale as old as time: amass a fortune with hard work, lose the fortune with reckless spending. That’s certainly true of Johnny Depp, whose latest movie, Ebenezer, is in theaters now on the 2026 movie schedule. Depp has gone through a lot of ups and downs in the last couple of decades, since becoming one of the highest-paid actors in Hollywood with the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise, starting in the summer of 2003. Now, a upcoming biography about Depp is getting into some of the details of his fortune made and lost, and the numbers, as you might expect, are staggering.

Sources indicate that in the fresh book, The Many Faces of Johnny Depp, author Mark Seal notes that court documents from 2017 let us in on just how staggering the numbers are. Depp has admitted to being hundreds of millions in the hole, but the new book touches more on where that money went and how he spent so much, so promptly. Of course, there are quite a few reasons, but they can be summed up in two, according to Seal. He writes (via PageSix):.

His vast wealth had been gutted, fittingly, in a Jack Sparrow-like bacchanal of excessive spending and financial mismanagement.

That spending, according to PageSix, included buying a luxury yacht, 14 homes, pricey cases of wine, jewelry, and a private island in the Bahamas. He also spent lavishly on travel and the people who surrounded him at the height of his earnings and fame. Seal writes:.

[He] didn’t move without an entourage and could never again fly on a commercial airline … He was no longer merely Johnny — he was Johnny Depp, mega-movie star, icon, brand, and franchise, with an expanding army of people depending on him for their livelihoods.

As Depp has admitted, he was also on the hook for $100 million in back taxes owed to Uncle Sam, a debt he blamed on the accountants and advisors he thought were paying the taxes when they apparently weren’t.

In the years since his court battle with Amber Heard, Depp’s reputation has taken a major hit, and that has also impacted his finances. For Ebenezer, Depp took a major cut from what he was earning for movies a decade ago. He apparently earned a “mere” $5 million for the fresh take on A Christmas Carol. That’s a lot of coin, for sure, but when you compare that to the $90 million Depp reportedly earned for Dead Men Tell No Tales, and the $16 million paycheck he received for Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald (a movie he was promptly cut from), you get the full picture.

The entertainment and sports worlds are filled with stories like this, and Depp isn’t all that unique, though the numbers involved are still eye-popping. There are also growing rumors that Depp could eventually return as Jack Sparrow, but that seems a long way off, even if they are true. Time will tell if Depp can ever start earning money like he used to.

According to recent reports, we cross-checked a list of 34 names supplied to us by the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain - the same organisation taking action against Rockstar on behalf of the fired employees. And of those names, we found 28 direct matches in the credits, along with a couple of discrepancies we've since verified, and some close-sounding names we're attempting to clarify. Some names may simply be missing. We won't publish the list for privacy reasons.

A number of those fired employees are seeking compensation for unfair dismissal amid allegations of "union busting", in an employment tribunal that comes to an end today. The delayed climax of the case couldn't be more fateful, aligned as it is with tomorrow's release of GTA 6, and the outcome will be historic either way.

It's a game that's wowed critics - Eurogamer awarded GTA 6 five stars in our review this afternoon - and which observers expect to generate $2bn in revenue in its opening weekend alone.

Industry observers note that but perhaps Christian Donlan put it best when digesting the opulence on display in the Netflix 'extended look' GTA 6 trailer. "To spend all this money making something so beautifully rich and detailed, to pay billions for this game and sweat every little animation, to float it out to us on Netflix, amongst genuine discussion around whether Netflix can handle it? In a recent development, valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability patch. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

In a recent development, it's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build fresh ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

Recent findings suggest that one could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

Of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained.".

"We anticipate having more information to share come January.".

Latest Update: Garmin Cyclists Can Now Make Themselves Appear on Waze in Real Time

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (466 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.
  • For riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a new layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists.
  • In a recent development, riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.

For riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a new layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists. The feature is rolling out now, but you should be aware of its limitations.

In a recent development, riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect. After that, sharing starts automatically when an outdoor cycling activity begins and stops when the ride ends. While a ride is underway, Waze customers near the cyclist see a cyclist icon move along the road and receive a Live Cycling Alert reminding them to slow down and stay aware.

The feature runs on LiveTrack, Garmin's existing live location-sharing tool, which lets friends and family follow a rider's real-time location, speed, course, and more. Garmin claims this collaboration extends that peace of mind to motorists, giving them greater awareness of their surroundings.

Garmin notes its location sharing is temporary and session-based. The rider's name, identity, and route are hidden, and no personal information is shared or displayed in Waze. Drivers see only an anonymous icon and the alert.

You'll need a few things to get this feature up and running:.

A compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin watch.

A phone running Garmin Connect with a data connection.

An outdoor cycling activity (the feature doesn't apply to indoor rides).

The good news is using the feature is free: LiveTrack costs nothing on compatible Garmin bike computers and watches, and Waze is free for drivers.

This fresh feature is a great safety perk, but there are real-world caveats worth considering:.

It has been revealed that this feature is for Waze only. Alerts reach drivers only when Waze is open on their phone. Google Maps, which has far more users, is excluded, so a large portion of the drivers you share the road with won't see you this way.

It depends on your phone's signal. Your position travels from the Garmin to your phone, then to Garmin's servers, then to Waze, and finally to the driver's phone. On a patchy rural signal, a few seconds of lag could put the icon on the wrong side of a bend from where you actually are. A rider who leaves their phone at home or whose phone loses signal simply won't show up on a Waze map, as a ride without a data connection is invisible to Waze.

Finally, remember to treat this safety feature as an extra perk, not a guarantee. At the end of the day, it isn't a replacement for bike lights, bright clothing, and defensive riding.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is presently the best-reviewed game of all time. Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off?

According to recent reports, well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an key insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the organization for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher.

By retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. We've seen that same kind of continuity at other studios who've delivered some of the last decade's biggest hits: FromSoft director Hidetaka Miyazaki has attributed its wins with Elden Ring and Armored Core 6 to its developers growing with the studio, while the breakout sales successes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2 were delivered by developers who'd spent years sharpening their craft at Larian and Arrowhead.

That lesson—that making successful games is easier when you keep the people who know how to make games around—isn't one that the games industry at large has been adhering to: In its latest game developer survey, GDC reported that 34% of its respondents had been laid off in the last two years. 20% of laid-off respondents said they'd been laid off twice or more in 24 months.

From Halo to Dragon Age, we've seen how beloved game franchises can suffer when their studios endure employment turmoil. After it laid off 1,600 Xbox workers in July, Microsoft's own employees noted that myopic job cuts at major game companies were weakening the games industry as a whole by dismantling its ability to produce quality games.

It's a bell we've been ringing a lot around here.

Recent findings suggest that still, while Rockstar boasts a deep roster of veteran employees, those devs aren't confident that they won't be the next ones suffering from mass layoffs: We've seen plenty of successful introduces lead to job cuts in recent years. As the company enjoys GTA 6's record-breaking launch, fears like those are why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are at the moment voting on unionization.

PSA: Some GTA 6 Ultimate Edition content is only available for the first chapter, and you'll have to put in hard graft to unlock more

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag.
  • As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.
  • Sources indicate that rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with new items uncovered behind each chapter".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag. So much so that Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent organization Take-Two, recently confirmed it's the edition most people are buying - and that's despite a lack of specific information about how its unlockable content works. With GTA 6 just hours away from release, however - and out now in certain parts of the work - details are beginning to emerge, and the answer is perhaps a little surprising.

As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.

Sources indicate that rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with new items uncovered behind each chapter". The specifics of how - and when - all this stuff unlocks, though, remained unclear. So if you've opted for the Ultimate Edition, you might be wondering where your stuff is when you finally fire up the game. As reported by IGN, which has full unlock details, it turns out virtually all of GTA 6's Ultimate Edition content, as per details in the in-game shop, requires progressing through the main story - in some cases dozens and dozens of hours into the story - before it'll become available.

Sources indicate that ultimate Edition-exclusive shops, for instance, unlock during Chapter 1, and many of the other additions become available by the end of Chapter 2. That doesn't sound too difficult, but as Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell notes, reaching that point could take upward of 25 hours. As for some of the late-game unlocks, such as the Shitzu Squalo and the Vice City Style outfits and tattoos (available in Chapter 4) and Chapter 5's 95 Grotti Cheetah, you could be looking at closing in on 60 hours of playtime before they unlock.

"It'll vary depending how hard people focus on the main story," Chris explains, "but if you were mostly focused on the main story plus the optional character-based missions in largely chronological order, that's about how long it'd take.".

It's also worth noting - perhaps surprisingly - that some Ultimate Edition content is only a temporary unlock, usable only during specific chapters. Jason's Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak, for instance, can only be accessed and enjoyed during Chapter 1. That's also true for his retro Vapid Ganado, available from the Coastal Auto Care mod shop in Key Lento. So basically, you'll want to make the most of these while you can!

All this might be a little disappointing for players who were expecting to be showered with Ultimate Edition spoils from the off (and that they'd be permanent unlocks), but the good news is 60 hours in GTA 6 is far from a chore. As Chris explained in his five star GTA 6 review, Rockstar's latest is an "irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action" that "pushes back the horizon of video games once again".

10 Movies Like ‘Interstellar’ You Should Watch Next

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: big sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing.
  • Industry observers note that if you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you.
  • In a recent development, if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: big sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing. Grounded in the intensity of the human experience, this story of humanity’s potential extinction and the sacrifice of one man to save it doesn’t just deliver exotic planets and thrilling spaceship maneuvers; it also provides all the feels as Joseph Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) sacrifices everything he has in an effort to save the entire human race. It’s one of the best science fiction films ever made, with Nolan’s signature complexity, time manipulations, and emotional wallop. If you love this movie, here are ten more that offer a similar viewing experience.

Industry observers note that if you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you. Stanley Kubrick’s 1968 epic (written by sci-fi master Arthur C. Clarke) traces humanity’s development from mildly smart apes to spacefaring capitalists who discover a mysterious obelisk on the Moon that sparks a mission to Jupiter. While it operates in a colder emotional key than Nolan’s film, 2001: A Space Odyssey absolutely delivers on the epic side of things (and the cool—if slightly deranged and deadly—artificial intelligences). Stream 2001: A Space Odyssey on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop. When the Sun begins to dim due to the interference of an alien entity, scientists identify the one nearby star that isn’t being similarly affected. Brilliant molecular biologist Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) winds up forced to go on what is assumed to be a fatal, one-way mission into deep space to try to find a way to save humanity, unexpectedly assisted by a charming alien he names Rocky. It’s got the same emotional volume and significant ideas as Interstellar, and fans of Nolan’s film will love it. Stream Project Hail Mary on MGM+ or Philo, or rent it on Prime Video.

Part of what makes Interstellar so compelling is the stakes: The human race is slowly dying, and a handful of people must make incredible sacrifices to save it. That’s the vibe of Sunshine, set in a future where the Sun is dimming and a spacecraft is dispatched to deliver an enormous bomb designed to reignite the Sun’s fusion cycle. But the mission is the second attempt after the first ship vanished mysteriously seven years earlier, and when the latest crew stumbles on the derelict wreck of the first mission, things quickly descend into violence and madness—but the crew remains determined to save the world, no matter the cost. Rent Sunshine on Prime Video.

In a recent development, interstellar works in large part because of the emotional dynamics at play. McConaughey’s character leaves his children behind and is forced to witness them growing up without him, missing out on their lives and saddled with the knowledge that they resent him despite the necessity of his mission. Arrival is a First Contact story focused on language—linguist Louise Banks (Amy Adams) is drafted into an effort to understand the strange, complex language of the aliens. As she slowly builds to an understanding of how the aliens communicate and perceive time itself, her own heartbreak and loss come into play, giving this film a similarly devastating emotional punch. Stream Arrival on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Family dynamics and the toll of lonely space missions fuel Ad Astra, a film with the same emotional core as Interstellar. Twenty-nine years ago, famed astronaut Clifford McBride (Tommy Lee Jones) led the Lima Project, a space station around Neptune searching for intelligent life. Thirteen years ago, Earth lost contact with him. When bursts of energy emanating from Neptune threaten to end life on Earth, his son, Roy (Brad Pitt), is dispatched to try to make contact with his father. It’s an epic journey with a powerful climax that will satisfy fans of Interstellar in every way. Stream Ad Astra on Netflix or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that ridley Scott’s prequel to Alien has its flaws, but if you’re looking for a sense of epic spacefaring adventure in the same key as Interstellar, it’s perfect. When two scientists discover a star map apparently left behind by ancient aliens, they secure funding from the Wayland Corporation to organize a space expedition to the indicated planet. Accompanied by a colorful crew and the android David, they discover an apparently abandoned outpost of the species dubbed the Engineers. The story wrestles with questions about humanity’s origins, purpose, and potential—but this being an Alien film, things quickly turn horrifying. Rent Prometheus on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, adapted from Carl Sagan’s 1985 novel, Contact follows astronomer Dr. Ellie Arroway (Jodie Foster), who becomes involved with an effort to decipher a signal originating from the star Vega. The signal turns out to be a set of instructions for constructing a one-person spacecraft of some kind, and Arroway is eventually selected as the candidate to take the journey. There’s a sense of courage in the face of the unknown that’s similar to Interstellar, as well as the thrill of strapping into a spaceship and pressing the ignition. Plus, there’s the added bonus of seeing one of the greatest trick shots in cinematic history. Rent Contact on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that stanislaw Lem’s 1961 novel Solaris explores what Lem saw as the impossibility of ever understanding a truly alien life. The two major adaptations—Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 version and Steven Soderbergh’s 2002 take starring George Clooney—are both worth watching, but Tarkovsky’s film is a masterpiece of psychological horror. The story is set mainly aboard a space station orbiting a planet covered in what appears to be a sentient "ocean" and chronicles the strange haunting and inexplicable experiences of the humans living on the station. If your favorite part of Interstellar is the ending when things get trippy and weird, you’ll probably love Solaris. Stream Solaris on HBO Max, Plex, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, the story of a mission to Jupiter’s moon Europa to search for intelligent life, Europa Report has the same sense of terrifying excitement that accompanies Interstellar’s missions to the different candidate planets. Leaning into the fragility of life in an environment not designed to support it, the mission crew face a steady stream of loss and danger as they work to catch sight of alien life on the frozen, deadly moon, ultimately faced with making terrifying sacrifices in order to provide humanity with the answers that it seeks. Stream Europa Report on Netflix, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that A film based on a 1956 epic science fiction poem written by a Swedish Nobel Laureate might seem like an unlikely match for fans of Interstellar, but it’s actually perfect. As the Earth becomes uninhabitable, humanity begins launching ships to colonize Mars. When one such ship, the Aniara, is damaged and veers irreversibly off course, the passengers and crew are faced with the knowledge that they will sail off into the void without hope of rescue. Within a few years, despair has driven some to suicide and madness, while others cling to the possibility that they might yet find a way back. The film offers a different perspective on the existential crisis of humanity’s extinction, exploring the worst-case scenario to its bitter, bleak end. Stream Aniara on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that breaking and entering is more complicated than it's ever been before in a Grand Theft Auto game. You never know what's behind a locked door – cash to be grabbed, narcotics to be fences, safes to be broken into. The problem is that breaking open doors creates a lot of noise, and will set off alarms. Thankfully, there is another way. All you need is to find the Snap Gun in GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that the Snap Gun is a lockpicking device that can be acquired by progressing through the main story, and it's perhaps the most crucial piece of equipment in the game (beating out the Slim Jim and the Key Cloner). Below I'm going to walk you through how to get the GTA 6 Snap Gun and how to use it.

Industry observers note that the Snap Gun is locked behind progression. You'll need to complete Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3, a fence-specific GTA 6 mission that unlocks after you've completed Boobie Time. You'll be introduced to Yasmani, one of the key vendors in GTA 6 who will pay a premium for marked bills and jewellery you've stolen. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that Jason and Lucia can properly assist in a few heists of high-end jewellery stores in Vice City.

Sources indicate that if a door is locked, there's a very good chance that you can use the Snap Gun to open it. Walk up to a door and, rather than pressing Square/X to break it open, press Triangle/Y instead. This will let you use the Snap Gun, where you're then required to use the left analogue stick to find the sweet spot and then pump the right-trigger until a meter fills. You'll hear the click when the lock is picked.

According to recent reports, the Snap Gun is particularly useful when you're robbing Pawn Shops, Jewellery stores, and other key locations – so long as you've already threatened the clerks and guards to stay still while you work. The Snap gun circumvents alarm systems installed in stores to monitor the door.

According to recent reports, it's worth noting here that in certain locations that carry a lot of cash or valuables, a Snap Gun won't be enough. If you walk up to a door and it's only asking for explosives, then a sticky bomb or grenade is what's required – just prepared for the alarms to go off and for the cops to be in hot pursuit.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's at the moment launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.
  • Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that don't expect GTA 6 to get an update supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles. Rockstar has explained that even the most powerful console of the bunch, the PS5 Pro, isn't powerful enough to run the lavish game at 40FPS or 60FPS.

Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's at the moment launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Like countless other significant productions this generation, the hope was that Rockstar Games would offer both quality and performance modes for its lush open-world monster.

Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.

"While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," the studio's technology production director, Marc Chambers, said in a statement to Kotaku. There you have it, then - even the beefiest console around can't handle Leonida at higher framerates.

Recent findings suggest that chambers did note some of the souped up console's other technical improvements, however: "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity.".

The tech gurus over at Digital Foundry gave some more insight into how GTA 6 runs on current-gen machines, calling it a "technical tour de force," though one that can still dip below 30FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X during busier chase scenes and explosive shootouts. It's perhaps unsurprising, then, that higher framerates are off the table for now.

In a recent development, A 30FPS launch is by no means a departure for Rockstar Games, either. GTA 5 also ran at an unsteady 30FPS when it first dropped onto the Xbox 360 and PS3, with 60FPS support only coming alongside the game's PC port more than a year later. I'm not too fussed about the game's 30FPS target, personally. I'd much rather have a game that consistently hits 30FPS than one that continuously chugs trying to reach 60FPS, especially when it's as frequently drop dead gorgeous as GTA 6.

The slightly lower framerates haven't affected the game's critical response so far, either. In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, our Chris Tapsell called it a "game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale" as "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again.".

If you're planning to jump into the game at midnight - or if you're virtually travelling to New Zealand for early entry - there's a few things to be aware of. First is that you won't be able to replay GTA 6's missions without multiple save files, so be sure to soak it all up. Second, some Ultimate Edition content is only available in the first chapter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. He's a good sport when I make him wear the dumbest graphic tees I can find. For a gunslinging drug runner, he's a gentle soul. I just have one complaint.

In a recent development, the man's got a leisurely gait. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button.

Sources indicate that to change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings, move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. The setting you're looking for is Movement Speed.

It has been revealed that this doesn't affect your top speed while sprinting and burning stamina. What it adjusts is the speed you move at when you fully push the joystick. There are four options, each one offering more speed than the last: Walk (the default), Fast Walk, Jog, and Run.

According to recent reports, it's a nice bit of granularity. I go with Fast Walk to give just a slight bump in my base speed without feeling like I'm rushing, but Jog or Run are good options if you really want to cover ground. Whichever one you choose, you can still voluntarily move at a slower pace by only slightly tilting the joystick.

There's also a Combat Movement Speed setting, which—as you might expect—changes the pace you walk at in a gunfight. There are only three options here: Fast Walk, Jog, and Run, because nobody wants to move slowly when they're actively being shot at.

It has been revealed that while you're in the menus, I'd recommend digging around to inspect all the available options. Rockstar included a lot of toggles and tweaks for fine-tuning how GTA 6 handles. You can even turn off vehicle damage altogether, if you don't want to pay for car repairs. Not that I've ever crashed or anything. Don't ask my mechanic.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

According to recent reports, that's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In a recent development, in GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

Recent findings suggest that the way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

According to recent reports, with each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

There's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

According to recent reports, we'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

According to recent reports, motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the manufacturer trumpeted that their "fresh operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft announced at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up newly introduced possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot said.

You'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec said. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing strategy with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.".

Industry observers note that that'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the tech giant affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

#51666. The Apple Watch's Newly introduced 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1365 w)

The Apple Watch's Newly introduced 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1365 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple declared in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on.
  • It has been revealed that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything.
  • According to recent reports, the recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple declared in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that launched at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

It has been revealed that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

According to recent reports, the recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":.

Recent findings suggest that music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

It has been revealed that sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this rolled out in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

Live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?

I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just stated in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

But Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an patch on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel plans, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all.

After you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

In a recent development, as promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was mentioned. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct.

Sources indicate that but still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people stated to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.).

Because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

It has been revealed that when it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

Details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

But it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

Recent findings suggest that I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most notable points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

And there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

In a recent development, it's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another organization's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

Sources indicate that "Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

Recent findings suggest that for the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a firm mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you're looking to upgrade the quality of the car you're driving around Leonida in, there's a good chance you're wondering how to clone keys in GTA 6.
  • With that in mind, I'm going to explain how to get the GTA 6 Key Cloner and how you can use it to steal more expensive vehicles.
  • The GTA 6 Key Cloner isn't available until you progress into Chapter 3 of the GTA 6 Mission list.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're looking to upgrade the quality of the car you're driving around Leonida in, there's a good chance you're wondering how to clone keys in GTA 6. While you can steal basic vehicles right from the beginning of the game, either by smashing the window or using a slim jim, keyless cars require specialist equipment before you're able to make off with the ride.

With that in mind, I'm going to explain how to get the GTA 6 Key Cloner and how you can use it to steal more expensive vehicles.

The GTA 6 Key Cloner isn't available until you progress into Chapter 3 of the GTA 6 Mission list. It's the 17th main story mission where you'll be asked to Steal the Zorrusso For Randy, a upcoming vehicle fence who will pay top-dollar for luxury cars and will even ask you to collect rare vehicles on his behalf.

Recent findings suggest that to do that, you'll need to be able to clone keys in GTA 6. Randy will install the Key Cloner application on your phone as part of this mission. It isn't possible to clone keys until you have reached this point.

According to recent reports, with the Key Cloner application installed on your phone, you're now able to get inside nicer cars and drive them away. Use the WAiNK app on your phone by holding Up on the D-pad to identify whether a car requires a key cloner to get inside, and whether the vehicle has any security trackers.

It has been revealed that so long as you have the Key Cloner, just walk up to the driver's side door and press Triangle/Y to begin cloning the key. You'll need to rotate the right-thumbstick until you find the sweet spot, which will be indicated by a lour whirring sound and rumble in your controller. You're now able to get inside without setting off the car alarm.

Sources indicate that just because you can get inside a keyless vehicle easily enough, it doesn't mean that there aren't consequences. This class of vehicle will typically have trackers installed, which can be identified by pressing up on the D-pad once you're behind the wheel (look underneath the vehicle name).

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Standard Trackers are easy enough to deal with, so long as you don't attract the attention of the police. It's worth noting that you are restricted from making modifications to cars with standard trackers, at least until you drive them to Randy's garage and register it as a personal vehicle in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that advanced Trackers are more of a problem. These will ping your exact location to cops as soon as you begin to drive too slowly. You also won't be able to fence (or own) this class of vehicle until you've progressed far enough through Randy's Wish List of stolen cars – Advanced Trackers are too hot to handle until then.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every time I see a newly introduced headline about yet another system outage this week, the beat of “We Didn’t Start the Fire” starts playing in my head: “Microsoft, NSA, grounded planes from FAA / United Airlines, Chase Bank, can’t send funds on Apple Pay…”.

Sources indicate that it feels like I could write a parody verse a day at the rate our infrastructure is faltering. A few weeks ago I wrote about the spate of cybersecurity incidents that led the industry to label last month “Black October.” Now my phone is blowing up, with everyone from colleagues to high school friends asking, what the hell is going on out there?

Are we under attack by a rogue nation? Are outdated software systems suddenly all throwing in the towel? Is this all just cyber-business as usual, with an unusually on-edge public?

I’m inclined to believe it’s some combination of all of the above. The FBI issued an urgent warning today that bad actors have been using ARTEX, the open-source AI penetration testing platform, to attempt widespread attacks. A source at a financial services manufacturer tells me, “It’s been a miserable month…. Just constant probing and hacking attempts.” Companies—and especially government agencies—with outdated software systems are scrambling to patch these vulnerabilities, and are often unable to do so securely without taking their systems entirely offline.

Recent findings suggest that “What used to take a skilled operator days or weeks of chaining is now happening in hours,” claims Snehal Antani, cofounder and CEO of the cybersecurity firm Horizon3. In other words: With AI, bad actors can pretty easily jiggle every doorknob around the globe to see who’s left their doors unlocked.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the total lack of clarity from the Trump administration hasn’t exactly been reassuring. Even one administration-aligned VC partner I spoke with this morning called the joint presser between Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin a “clown show.”.

For now, I’d urge you to heed the same advice I gave last time I wrote about this: Make sure those passwords are airtight and that multifactor authentication is activated. And maybe, just maybe, stock up on some light supplies you’d like to have around if 21st-century services stop working the way they’re supposed to.

“Going forward, expect this to become normal rather than exceptional,” Antani tells me. “We should expect persistent disruption of digital services—travel, banking, commerce, etc.—in the coming months as these organizations scramble to quickly improve their cyber resilience.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private.
  • It has been revealed that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

It has been revealed that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access.

Many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Sources indicate that reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

A multireddit is a feed that highlights posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in new Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

Sources indicate that if you want to reduce Reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

Industry observers note that reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by new, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

After all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As declared in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

According to recent reports, kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

It has been revealed that fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:.

"We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you demonstrated us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul.".

Condolences to Kurabayashi's family.

Breaking: 10 Hacks Every Hulu User Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations.
  • Recent findings suggest that another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain indicates.
  • If you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations. "Disliking" a show or movie removes it from your Home view and You May Also Like entirely, so the only way you'll see that content is if you search for it. You can dislike on the Details page if you're watching on your TV or use the thumbs down on mobile or web. (The "Like" button will obviously influence your algorithm in the opposite way). If your "Continue Watching" queue is cluttered with demonstrates you started but didn't like enough to finish, you can remove them from your watch history as well as the My Stuff list. This, too, will allow content to remain searchable but not suggested in other areas of the app.

Recent findings suggest that another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain indicates. This keeps content from influencing your recommendations and prevents other viewers from seeing what's in your watch history or saved content (especially if there are things you want to keep private).

If you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it. Hulu allows you to adjust the color and opacity of the font, background, and window so you get the right contrast, and you can also select the specific font and font scaling. On your streaming device, go to Settings > Subtitles & Captions, then hit the back button on your remote to save your preferences. You can update these settings on mobile and desktop as well.

Recent findings suggest that if you have a long list of shows and films to watch but can't decide what to start next, look for the "Expiring Soon" badge to see which titles are leaving the service in the next two weeks. Badges display the number of days remaining, so you can determine what to prioritize and whether it's worth diving in based on how much time you have to finish before the expiration date. Go to "My Stuff" to monitor saved titles that are expiring soon.

If you've been watching Hulu under an account shared with family or friends and need to switch to your own subscription, you can transfer your profile to keep your watch history and settings intact instead of starting from scratch. You can initiate a profile transfer on a TV-connected device. Note that account holders have to approve transfer requests within seven days, and once expired, transfer requests cannot be resubmitted—so be sure to let the primary user know that you've made the request.

Sources indicate that if you've shared your Hulu login information with friends or activated your account on devices you don't own, you may want to regularly audit where your account is being used and remove any that don't need access. This includes TVs in Airbnbs and hotels. If you stay logged in, unauthorized consumers may have access to your Hulu account and personal data. You can see activated devices (and their activation date) under Your Account > Watch Hulu on Your Devices > Manage Devices. Click Remove next to old or unrecognized devices.

Hulu has an offline mode that allows you to download shows and movies to watch when you don't have a network connection. This is useful for traveling or when you know your wifi or cell service will be limited. Downloads are only available on supported iOS and Android devices, which means you may have to consider how much space your content takes up. You can select High for video quality if you want maximum resolution, but you may want to choose Standard if you are short on storage. This option is available under Downloads > Settings > Video Quality on iOS and Account > Settings > Downloads > Video Quality on Android. Note that once you click play on downloaded content, you have 48 hours to watch it before it expires—so don't start it unless you are ready.

Sources indicate that if you have a Hulu + Live TV subscription, you must designate a "Home" network, which determines the local channels included in your initiative. You can update your location up to four times within a 12-month period, but this limitation is meant to prevent viewers outside a household from sharing a subscription. Hulu does allow you to stream live TV on mobile when you're away from your home network (within the U.S.) as long as you access your account on that network every 30 days. If you travel often, check in with your mobile device frequently to avoid being locked out when you're away. Note that you can still watch streaming content with no restrictions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • As pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the major release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles.
  • "Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is key.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

As pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the major release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

"Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is key. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either.".

Recent findings suggest that one day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe.".

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

In a recent development, now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

Recent findings suggest that so what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

In a recent development, this is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Significant Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

It has been revealed that have you tried robbing a bank or loan store in Vice City, and made off with a duffel bag of marked bills, only to find that Jason and Lucia get covered in pink paint once they've made a successful getaway? If you're sick of this happening to you, then you need to get yourself a Dye-Pack Jammer in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that this essential piece of equipment is used to disable the signal transmitted by dye-packs, which are attached to all marked bills from high-end robbery locations across Leonida. You'll know if you're at risk of getting marked – making yourself exceedingly obvious to patrolling cops, at least until you can change your appearance – because you'll hear a sharp beeping noise just before the explosion. It's classic GTA 6.

It has been revealed that you will unlock the GTA 6 Dye-Pack Jammer as part of the main story progression. You'll need to complete Credit Check, which is Chapter 3's 16th mission in GTA 6. You'll collect the equipment from a character named Karim, and it is not missable. This is the only way you can unlock the Dye-Pack Jammer in GTA 6.

Once you've unlocked the Dye-Pack Jammer in the Credit Check mission, you'll now be able to steal Marked Bills from Banks and Payday Loan locations. While it's possible to acquire Marked Bills before this, none of the GTA 6 fence locations will accept them and they will more often than not result in you getting pink dye all over your clothes.

Sources indicate that once you have the Dye-Pack Jammer, you're free to rob who and what you like. And you never need to fear the risk of getting covered in dye ever again. So it's well worth progressing early into Chapter 3 to get this item as soon as you're able to.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

Recent findings suggest that however, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we currently consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

According to recent reports, using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

In a recent development, now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

Last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

This does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

According to recent reports, we also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have mentioned about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

Thanks again, and happy voting!

The Nightingale First Look: Dakota and Elle Fanning on Their Long-Awaited First Film as Sisters
